newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end weak, bump against resistance.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end weak, bump against resistance.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed weak on Thursday after three days of consecutive record closes as the Hang Seng index unsuccessfully tried to tackle resistance at 13,200 points, brokers said.
The Hang Seng closed 67.60 points lower at 13,099.56, after a see-saw session which saw the index up at a record intra-day high of 13,237.73 at one point, then at a low of 13,028.03.
Turnover was a heavy HK$10.68 billion compared with HK$12.29 billion on Wednesday.
"It needs to correct. It wants to correct," said Miles Remington, sales trader at Crosby Securities.
"It hit technical resistance at 13,200...I think we possihly are going to find it difficult to get through there," he said.
Fears of share placements by blue chip companies also prompted some investors to take profits. Despite Thursday's loss, the Hang Seng index has risen 210.19 points this week.
"For the past few weeks we have been up, so today's correction is not unexpected," said Sunny Chan, senior research manager at Seapower Securities. "People are using placement fears to take profit."
Banking stocks took a hit on Thursday with HSBC Holdings closing HK$1.50 points lower at HK$157.00 and Hang Seng Bank off HK$1.75 at HK$90.75. Bank of East Asia finished HK$0.20 lower at HK$33.60.
"People are continually looking to switch out of larger banks, looking for better value in smaller second-line banks," said Remington. "There is selective switching in the market."
He said investors had also been switching out of Wheelock, which closed down HK$0.50 at HK$20.50, into Wharf, which rose HK$0.60 to HK$36.70.
However, property stocks were well supported. Henderson Land rose HK$1.00 to HK$75.75 and Sun Hung Kai Properties advanced HK$0.75 to HK$94.25.

Chan said lagging stocks were likely to lead the market higher from here. "I expect the market to test higher levels not on HongKong Bank or the developer stocks. I think it will be the laggard stocks like property investors, conglomerates that will lead the rise," he said.
Laggard Swire Pacific gained HK$1.25 to HK$72.25. Henderson Investment rose HK$0.20 to HK$9.05 and Amoy Properties rose HK$0.15 to HK$10.55.
